translation_en: ‘Abd Allah ibn Raja’ narrated to us: Shu‘bah informed us, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, that ‘A’ishah wanted to buy Barirah, but her patrons insisted on stipulating that the right of wala’ belong to them. She mentioned that to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and he said, ‘Buy her and set her free, for the right of wala’ belongs to the one who frees her.’ Meat was brought to the Prophet and it was said, ‘This was given as charity to Barirah.’ He said, ‘For her it is charity, and for us it is a gift.’ Adam narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us and added: She was given a choice concerning her husband.

Qutaybah narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to us, from Nafi‘, that when Ibn ‘Umar was asked about marrying a Christian or Jewish woman, he said, ‘Allah has forbidden polytheist women to the believers, and I know of no greater act of associating partners with Allah than a woman saying that her Lord is ‘Isa, who is one of Allah’s servants.’

Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us: Hisham informed us, from Ibn Jurayj. He said: ‘Ata’ narrated from Ibn ‘Abbas: The polytheists were of two kinds in relation to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and the believers: polytheists at war, whom he fought and who fought him; and polytheists with a treaty, whom he did not fight and who did not fight him. When a woman from among the enemy emigrated, she was not proposed to until she menstruated and became pure. Once she was pure, marriage to her was lawful. If her husband emigrated before she married, she was returned to him. If a male or female slave from among them emigrated, they became free and had the same status as the Emigrants. He then mentioned that the people of the treaty were treated as in Mujahid’s report. If a male or female slave belonging to treaty polytheists emigrated, they were not returned, and their price was returned to their former owners.’

‘Ata’ narrated from Ibn ‘Abbas: Qaribah bint Abi Umayyah was married to ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, who divorced her. Mu‘awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan then married her. Umm al-Hakam bint Abi Sufyan was married to ‘Iyad ibn Ghanm al-Fihri, who divorced her. ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Uthman al-Thaqafi then married her.

Ibn Bukayr narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab. Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir said: Ibn Wahb narrated to me: Yunus narrated to me. Ibn Shihab said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: When believing women emigrated to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, he tested them with Allah’s words, ‘O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them…’ (60:10), through the end of the verse. ‘A’ishah said: Any believing woman who acknowledged that condition had passed the test. When they acknowledged it in their statements, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said to them, ‘Go, for I have accepted your pledge.’ No, by Allah, the Messenger of Allah’s hand never touched a woman’s hand. He accepted their pledges only in words. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah required from women only what Allah had commanded him, saying to them in words, ‘I have accepted your pledge.’

Isma‘il ibn Abi Uways narrated to us, from his brother, from Sulayman, from Humayd al-Tawil, who heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, swore to stay away from his wives. His leg had been injured, so he stayed in an upper room of his for 29 nights. Then he came down. They said, ‘Messenger of Allah, you swore to stay away for a month.’ He said, ‘A month is 29 days.’

Qutaybah narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to us, from Nafi‘, that Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, used to say concerning the oath of abstention mentioned by Allah: After the period has expired, it is not lawful for the husband except to remain with his wife in a fair manner or resolve upon divorce, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded.

Isma‘il said to me: Malik narrated to me, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar: When four months have passed, the man is held until he divorces her. Divorce does not take effect against him until he divorces her. This is also reported from ‘Uthman, ‘Ali, Abu al-Darda’, ‘A’ishah, and 12 men among the Companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from Yazid, the freedman of al-Munba‘ith: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was asked about a lost sheep and said, ‘Take it, for it is either yours, your brother’s, or the wolf’s.’ He was asked about a lost camel. He became angry and his cheeks reddened, and he said, ‘What business do you have with it? It has its own shoes and water-skin; it drinks water and eats trees until its Lord finds it.’ He was asked about a lost item and said, ‘Learn its cord and container, announce it for a year, and if someone comes who recognizes it, give it to him; otherwise, mix it with your property.’ Sufyan said: I met Rabi‘ah ibn Abi ‘Abd al-Rahman—Sufyan said: I did not retain anything else from him—and asked, ‘Do you say that Yazid, the freedman of al-Munba‘ith, narrated this report about lost property from Zayd ibn Khalid?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ Yahya said that Rabi‘ah also related it from Yazid, the freedman of al-Munba‘ith, from Zayd ibn Khalid. Sufyan said: I met Rabi‘ah and said this to him.

‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Abu ‘Amir ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Amr narrated to us: Ibrahim narrated to us, from Khalid, from ‘Ikrimah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, circumambulated on his camel, and whenever he came to the Corner, he pointed toward it and said, ‘Allah is greatest.’ Zaynab said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘A breach this size has been opened in the barrier of Gog and Magog,’ and he curled his fingers to indicate 90.

Musaddad narrated to us: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us: Salamah ibn ‘Alqamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Abu al-Qasim, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘On Friday there is an hour when no Muslim is standing in prayer and asking Allah for something good but He gives it to him.’ He gestured with his hand, placing the tip of his middle finger on the joint of his little finger. We thought he was indicating how brief it is.

Al-Uwaysi said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d narrated to us, from Shu‘bah ibn al-Hajjaj, from Hisham ibn Zayd, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: During the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, a Jewish man attacked a young girl, took the silver ornaments she wore, and crushed her head. Her family brought her to the Messenger of Allah while she was near death and unable to speak. The Messenger of Allah said to her, ‘Did so-and-so kill you?’—naming someone other than the killer. She gestured with her head, ‘No.’ He asked about another man besides the killer, and she gestured, ‘No.’ Then he said, ‘Was it so-and-so?’—naming her killer—and she gestured, ‘Yes.’ The Messenger of Allah ordered that the man’s head be crushed between two stones.

Qabisah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say, ‘Fitnah is from over here,’ and he pointed toward the east.

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Jarir ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, who said: We were traveling with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. When the sun had set, he said to a man, ‘Get down and prepare a drink for me.’ The man said, ‘If only you would wait until it is evening.’ He said, ‘Get down and prepare a drink.’ The man said, ‘There is still daylight.’ Then he said, ‘Get down and prepare it.’ The man got down and prepared it for him the third time. The Messenger of Allah drank, then gestured with his hand toward the east and said, ‘When you see the night approaching from this direction, the fasting person has broken his fast.’

‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray‘ narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu ‘Uthman, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Mas‘ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Let none of you be prevented by Bilal’s call—or his announcement—from eating his pre-dawn meal. He calls—or announces—so that those of you who are standing in prayer may return and those sleeping may wake.’ This is not the call that indicates dawn—or morning.’ Yazid demonstrated with his hands, then held one apart from the other.

Al-Layth said: Ja‘far ibn Rabi‘ah narrated to me, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz, who said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘The example of a miser and a generous spender is like two men wearing coats of iron from their chests up to their collarbones. Whenever the generous spender gives anything, the coat stretches over his skin until it covers his fingertips and erases his tracks. As for the miser, whenever he intends to spend, every ring of the coat stays in its place. He tries to widen it, but it does not widen.’ He gestured with his finger toward his throat.

Qutaybah narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id al-Ansari, who heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Shall I tell you which clans of the Ansar are best?’ They said, ‘Yes, Messenger of Allah.’ He said, ‘Banu al-Najjar, then those closest to them, Banu ‘Abd al-Ashhal; then those closest to them, Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj; then those closest to them, Banu Sa‘idah.’ He gestured with his hand, closing his fingers and then spreading them as though throwing something, and said, ‘There is good in every clan of the Ansar.’

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Hazim said: I heard Sahl ibn Sa‘d al-Sa‘idi, a Companion of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say that the Messenger of Allah said, ‘My being sent and the Hour are like this and this’—or ‘like these two.’ He joined his index and middle fingers.

Adam narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us: Jabal ibn Suhaym narrated to us: I heard Ibn ‘Umar say that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘The month is like this, and this, and this’—meaning 30 days. Then he said, ‘And like this, and this, and this’—meaning 29 days. At times he counted 30 and at times 29.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Yahya ibn Sa‘id narrated to us, from Isma‘il, from Qays, from Abu Mas‘ud, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, pointed with his hand toward Yemen and said, ‘Faith is over here’—twice. ‘Indeed, harshness and hard-heartedness are among the loud camel herders, where the two horns of Satan rise: Rabi‘ah and Mudar.’

‘Amr ibn Zurarah narrated to us: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Abi Hazim informed us, from his father, from Sahl, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘I and the one who cares for an orphan will be in Paradise like this.’ He pointed with his index and middle fingers and held them slightly apart.

Yahya ibn Qaza‘ah narrated to us: Malik narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu Hurayrah, that a man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, a black boy has been born to me.’ He asked, ‘Do you have camels?’ The man said, ‘Yes.’ He asked, ‘What colors are they?’ He replied, ‘Red.’ He asked, ‘Is there a gray one among them?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ He asked, ‘How did that happen?’ He said, ‘Perhaps it inherited a strain.’ He said, ‘Perhaps this son of yours inherited a strain.’

Musa ibn Isma‘il narrated to us: Juwayriyah narrated to us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man from the Ansar accused his wife of adultery. The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had them both swear the prescribed oaths, then separated them.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me: Ibn Abi ‘Adi narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan: ‘Ikrimah narrated to us, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that Hilal ibn Umayyah accused his wife of adultery. He came and testified while the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was saying, ‘Allah knows that one of you is lying. Will either of you repent?’ Then she stood and testified.

Isma‘il narrated to us, saying: Malik narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, that Sahl ibn Sa‘d al-Sa‘idi informed him that ‘Uwaymir al-‘Ajlani came to ‘Asim ibn ‘Adi al-Ansari and said, ‘‘Asim, what do you think if a man finds another man with his wife? Should he kill him, in which case you would kill him, or what should he do? Ask the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, about it for me.’ ‘Asim asked the Messenger of Allah about it, but the Messenger of Allah disliked questions of that sort and criticized them, until what ‘Asim heard from him weighed heavily on him. When ‘Asim returned to his family, ‘Uwaymir came and said, ‘‘Asim, what did the Messenger of Allah say to you?’ ‘Asim said to ‘Uwaymir, ‘You have brought me nothing good. The Messenger of Allah disliked the question I asked him.’ ‘Uwaymir said, ‘By Allah, I will not stop until I ask him about it.’ He came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, among the people and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, what do you think if a man finds another man with his wife? Should he kill him, in which case you would kill him, or what should he do?’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘It has been revealed concerning you and your wife. Go and bring her here.’ Sahl said: They invoked curses upon one another while I was present with the people. When they had finished, ‘Uwaymir said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I would be lying about her if I kept her.’ He divorced her three times before the Messenger of Allah ordered him to do so. After they had finished invoking curses, he separated from her before the Messenger of Allah, who said, ‘That is the separation between every two spouses who invoke curses upon one another.’ Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Shihab said: The practice after them was to separate spouses who invoke curses upon one another. She was pregnant, and her son was attributed to his mother. The practice concerning inheritance was that she inherited from him and he inherited from her whatever Allah had prescribed for him. Ibn Jurayj said, from Ibn Shihab, from Sahl ibn Sa‘d al-Sa‘idi, concerning this report, that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘If she gives birth to a red, short child like a small lizard, I think she has spoken the truth and he has lied about her. If she gives birth to a black-eyed, dark-skinned child with large buttocks, I think he has spoken the truth about her.’ She gave birth to the kind he disliked.

Yahya narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Ibn Shihab informed me about the spouses who invoke curses and the practice concerning them, in the report of Sahl ibn Sa‘d, the brother of Banu Sa‘idah: An Ansari man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, what do you think if a man finds another man with his wife? Should he kill him, or what should he do?’ Allah revealed concerning his case what He mentioned in the Quran about spouses who invoke curses. The Prophet said, ‘Allah has decided concerning you and your wife.’ They invoked curses against one another in the mosque while I witnessed it. When they finished, he said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I would be lying about her if I kept her,’ and he divorced her three times before the Messenger of Allah ordered him to do so. When they had finished invoking curses, he separated from her in the presence of the Prophet, who said, ‘That is the separation between every two spouses who invoke curses upon one another.’ Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Shihab said: The practice afterward was to separate spouses who invoke curses upon one another. She was pregnant, and the child was attributed to his mother. The practice concerning inheritance was that she inherited from him and he inherited from her according to what Allah prescribed for him. Ibn Jurayj said, from Ibn Shihab, from Sahl ibn Sa‘d al-Sa‘idi, concerning this hadith: The Prophet said, ‘If she gives birth to a red, short child like a small lizard, I think she has spoken the truth and he has lied about her. If she gives birth to a black-eyed, dark-skinned child with large buttocks, I think he has spoken the truth about her.’ She gave birth to the kind he disliked.

Sa‘id ibn ‘Ufayr narrated to us, saying: Al-Layth narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: Mutual imprecation was mentioned in the presence of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. ‘Asim ibn ‘Adi made a comment about it and then left. A man from his people came to him complaining that he had found another man with his wife. ‘Asim said, ‘I have only been tested with this because of what I said.’ He took him to the Prophet and told him what he had found his wife doing. The man was yellow-complexioned, lean, and straight-haired, while the man he alleged he had found with his wife was dark-skinned, broad-bodied, and heavyset. The Prophet said, ‘O Allah, make it clear.’ The woman gave birth resembling the man her husband said he had found with her, so the Prophet had them invoke curses upon one another. A man in the gathering said to Ibn ‘Abbas, ‘Is she the woman about whom the Prophet said, “If I were to stone anyone without proof, I would stone her”?’ He replied, ‘No. That was a woman who openly displayed wrongdoing in Islam.’ Abu Salih and ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf said: ‘Khadhil’ means broad-bodied.

‘Amr ibn Zurarah narrated to me: Isma‘il informed us, from Ayyub, from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, who said: I asked Ibn ‘Umar about a man who accused his wife. He said, ‘The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, separated the two brothers of Banu al-‘Ajlan and said, “Allah knows that one of you is lying. Will either of you repent?” They both refused. He said it again, and they both refused. He said it a third time, and they refused, so he separated them.’ Ayyub said: ‘Amr ibn Dinar told me that there is something in the hadith that I do not see you narrating.’ He said: The man asked, ‘What about my property?’ He was told, ‘You have no property. If you have spoken truthfully, you had intercourse with her; if you have lied, it is even farther from you.’

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: ‘Amr said: I heard Sa‘id ibn Jubayr say: I asked Ibn ‘Umar about spouses who invoke curses. He said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said to them, ‘Your reckoning is with Allah. One of you is lying, and you have no claim against her.’ The man said, ‘What about my property?’ He said, ‘You have no property. If you have spoken truthfully about her, that was in return for the intimacy you had with her; if you have lied about her, it is even farther from you.’ Sufyan said: I memorized this from ‘Amr. Ayyub said: I heard Sa‘id ibn Jubayr say: I asked Ibn ‘Umar about a man who invoked curses against his wife. He gestured with two fingers—and Sufyan separated his index and middle fingers—and said, ‘The Prophet separated the two brothers of Banu al-‘Ajlan and said, “Allah knows that one of you is lying. Will either of you repent?”’ He said this three times. Sufyan said: I memorized it from ‘Amr and Ayyub as I have told you.

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to me: Anas ibn ‘Iyad narrated to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, from Nafi‘, that Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, informed him that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, separated a man from his wife after he accused her, and made them both swear oaths.
